issue: Receiver-leg dedupe excludes FAILED runs, so a persistently failing head is retried on every refire with no cooldown

verdicts.evidence: Dedupe confirmed at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1207 (tree): `.exclude(status__in=(ReviewRunStatus.SUPERSEDED, ReviewRunStatus.FAILED))`, so a FAILED run at the current head_sha is not treated as handled; execution then falls through to `_supersede_prior_runs` + `ReviewRun.objects...create(...)` + `_start_review_workflow` (tasks.py:1222-1234) — a fresh full review. No cooldown exists on this leg: `STAMPHOG_LABEL_REREVIEW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (tasks.py:78) is applied only on the label webhook path (tasks.py:1095). The trigger is genuinely repeated: review_hog's `handle_task_run_saved` fires on every TaskRun save touching `output` with a `pr_url` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:86-96, 126-139), and its docstring assumes a same-head refire "costs one fetch (early-exit)" — which stops being true once the run at that head is FAILED.
verdicts.notes: Real code behavior, exactly as described, but the claimed impact ("retried on every refire", "unbounded sandbox/LLM budget") is materially overstated. Mitigations visible in the tree: (1) refires arriving while a run at the head is QUEUED/GATED/REVIEWING/COMPLETED early-exit (tasks.py:1211-1221) — QUEUED/GATED/COMPLETED are the non-excluded statuses per facade/enums.py:19-26 — so a new attempt can only start after the prior run terminally FAILs via the workflow's `mark_review_failed` (temporal/activities.py:820), i.e. cadence is throttled to roughly one attempt per failed-review duration, not per output save; (2) total spend is bounded by the self-driving task's finite lifetime and save frequency; (3) sandbox cost per retry is only incurred if the deterministic failure happens after provisioning — an early fetch_context failure retries cheaply. Excluding FAILED is also a deliberate transient-recovery design (GitHub blips, sandbox hiccups should get another shot); the genuine gap is only the missing backoff/cap for the rarer deterministic-failure + continuous-refire combination. Valid low-priority hardening note (mirror the label-path cooldown per (pull_request, head_sha)), not a should_fix.

verdicts.evidence: tasks.py:1206-1207 — inbox dedup filters on (pull_request, head_sha) and excludes FAILED, so a FAILED run at the same head never satisfies `existing` and a new ReviewRun is created each fire; no attempt cap or cooldown exists. receivers.py:85-96,126-139 — receiver fires on every TaskRun save touching `output` with pr_url, gated only by the TaskRun's status; docstrings (receivers.py:5-7,77-79; tasks.py:1124-1128) confirm repeat saves with an unchanged head are expected and rely on the head-keyed dedupe to no-op, which FAILED runs escape. temporal/client.py:43 — workflow id `stamphog-review-{review_run_id}` is per-row, so each new row launches a fresh full sandbox+LLM+GitHub workflow. activities.py:820-847 — mark_review_failed runs after an unrecoverable (post-retry) workflow error, so deterministic failures recur on every relaunch. test_tasks.py:979 — `(FAILED, "sha-1", "new", 2)` codifies retry-after-FAILED as intended, but with no transient/deterministic distinction or budget.
verdicts.notes: Mechanism fully verified in this PR's new code. Mitigating nuance: relaunches are bounded by TaskRun output-save frequency (per agent turn), toggle- and assignee-gated, and transient failures self-heal — so it's uncapped resource amplification under a deterministic-failure precondition, not an infinite loop. The retry-after-FAILED is deliberately tested design for transient recovery; the missing piece is a per-(PR, head) attempt cap or cooldown. should_fix is the right severity.

this_experiment_findings.title: A FAILED run at the current head is re-created on every receiver refire, with no cap
this_experiment_findings.problem: The head-keyed dedupe excludes only `SUPERSEDED` and `FAILED`, so a run that reached `FAILED` at the current head makes every subsequent refire fall through to `_supersede_prior_runs` + create a fresh `QUEUED` run and Temporal workflow. The review_hog receiver deliberately re-fires on every `TaskRun` output save (its docstring: "Repeat saves with an unchanged target re-fire it deliberately"), and the follow-up loop saves output repeatedly while babysitting the PR. So one persistently failing review (bad sandbox image, engine crash, gateway outage) produces one new full sandbox + LLM attempt per TaskRun save for as long as the loop keeps saving, with no per-head attempt cap. Transient-failure retry is clearly intended (the docstring's "refire after a head the webhook leg never delivered still reviews the new commits" covers a lost head, and FAILED exclusion covers retries), but the unbounded version is a cost and noise hazard, and each failed attempt also stays in run history.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Bound the retry: for example, treat a recently failed run at the same head as a dedupe hit (add a time window, e.g. skip if the newest FAILED run at this head is younger than N minutes), or record an attempt counter in `run.output` and stop re-creating after K attempts per (PR, head). The webhook leg has delivery-id dedupe and Celery `max_retries=3`; the receiver leg currently has neither bound on this path.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim: the receiver-leg head-keyed dedupe excludes FAILED, so a persistently failing head spawns a fresh run on every refire with no cap or cooldown.

fresh_votes.evidence: Code path confirmed: products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py `handle_task_run_saved` drops creates and any save whose update_fields lacks "output". When the stamphog toggle is on, it queues `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149), which calls `process_inbox_pr_review`. In products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1221 the dedupe skips SUPERSEDED and FAILED runs, so a FAILED run at the current head leads to `_supersede_prior_runs` and a new QUEUED run. So the mechanism is real. But it is deliberate and tested: products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:979/986 has the case "failed_run_recreated_on_refire", and its comment at lines 997-999 says so a single-commit PR whose one review died isn't permanently stranded.
fresh_votes.refutation:
The finding's key premise is that output saves fire again and again while the follow-up loop watches the PR. Nothing in the repo shows that. The TaskRun output writers I found are:
- set_task_run_output: facade/api.py:2139-2154.
- The run PATCH, which saves output only when the caller sends output: facade/api.py:~2040-2066.
- webhooks.py:276 `_record_run_output_field`, which writes each key once and returns early when the key is already set.
The temporal workflows never write output. The receiver docstring says the agent server syncs head_branch only at the end of a turn "whose current branch changed", and pr_url is written once. So after the PR opens, output saves are rare events, not a per-turn stream.

Each refire also re-fetches the PR and exits when it is no longer open (tasks.py:1166-1169). The receiver skips FAILED or CANCELLED task runs. `_supersede_prior_runs` leaves only one live run.

So a persistently failing review is retried roughly once per rare output save, not without limit. Retry on refire is the tested design choice, which makes the missing cap speculative hardening sized for an unlikely scenario, not a defect.

fresh_votes.evidence:
The FAILED exclusion at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1207 is on purpose, and a test pins it. products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:979/986 is the parametrized case `failed_run_recreated_on_refire`, where (FAILED, same head) expects a new run. Its comment at lines 995-998 gives the reason: "A FAILED run doesn't count as handled: the refire recreates it, so a single-commit PR whose one review died isn't permanently stranded without a verdict."

The finding says the follow-up loop saves output again and again while it babysits the PR. The code does not show that. products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:79-85 drops any save whose declared update_fields does not include "output", and the comment there says "follow-up state persistence, status flips" go through that path. It also returns early for FAILED or CANCELLED TaskRuns (line 86).

Every TaskRun save I found declares its update_fields:
- tasks/temporal/client.py:76 and update_task_run_status.py:69 save status fields.
- models.py:1263 saves state.
- facade/api.py:2075 adds "output" only when the PATCH carries output (line 2044).
- set_task_run_output (api.py:2154) and the webhook backstop (webhooks.py:292) are the output writers.

Output is written when the PR opens, when the webhook backstop runs, and when an agent turn changes the branch (receivers.py:27-29). None of these runs in a loop at the same head. A new push changes the head, so the same-head retry path no longer applies and the dedupe handles it normally. So the retry count is limited by a handful of output writes, not unlimited. The refire also re-checks at tasks.py:1166 that the PR is still open.
fresh_votes.refutation: Two things undercut the claim. First, retrying at a head whose run FAILED is intended and tested (test_tasks.py:979-998). Second, the claimed trigger, output saves that repeat without end at an unchanged head, is not supported by the code. The receiver skips saves whose declared fields exclude output (receivers.py:79-85), and TaskRun output is written only at a few discrete events (api.py:2154, webhooks.py:292, the API PATCH with output). What is left is a guess about retry cost, not a defect that can be triggered.

fresh_votes.evidence:
The mechanism itself is accurate. At products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1221 the head-keyed dedupe skips SUPERSEDED and FAILED runs, so a refire at the same head after a FAILED run creates a new QUEUED run and starts a new workflow. The claimed trigger rate is what fails.

1. Saves that skip `output` never reach this task. products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:79-83 returns early when `update_fields` is set and does not include "output". The comment there names follow-up state persistence and status flips as the saves it drops. receivers.py:84-85 also skips TaskRuns that are FAILED or CANCELLED.
2. The stamphog task is only queued when `output.pr_url` is set (receivers.py:127). It goes through on_commit and the facade at products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155.
3. The backend never writes TaskRun.output in a loop. A grep of products/tasks/backend/temporal (process_task and execute_sandbox activities) finds no output writes, so the PR follow-up workflow does not save output. Only three paths write it:
   - `set_task_run_output` at products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2154, the agent's `set_output` endpoint.
   - The run PATCH merge at facade/api.py:2039-2075.
   - `_record_run_output_field` at products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:276-298. It is idempotent: it returns False when the key already exists, so it writes pr_url and pr_merged once each.
4. After the PR is merged or closed, tasks.py:1166-1169 returns before the dedupe, so the pr_merged save cannot start a review.
5. The receiver docstring (receivers.py:23-31) says the agent server syncs `head_branch` only on turns where the current branch changed. That is a rare event, not one save per follow-up turn.

So a head that stays FAILED gets one retry per real output-carrying save. That is a handful of saves over a PR's life, not an unbounded stream. Retrying a FAILED run on a new signal is also the intended recovery. The webhook path does the same exclusion (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:548).
fresh_votes.refutation:
The finding depends on "the follow-up loop saves output repeatedly while babysitting the PR". The code contradicts this:
- The receiver drops saves whose `update_fields` omit "output" (receivers.py:79-83).
- No Temporal follow-up activity writes TaskRun.output.
- Webhook output writes happen once per key (webhooks.py:283-289).
- pr_merged saves hit the not-open early return (tasks.py:1166-1169).

That leaves only agent `set_output` or PATCH calls that carry pr_url, plus head_branch changes. These are rare and bounded, so no reachable production path loops re-creating runs without limit. What remains is a bounded retry of a failed review, which the design intends.

this_experiment_findings.title: Repeated receiver fires re-create review runs for a FAILED head with no cooldown
this_experiment_findings.problem: The head-keyed dedupe excludes FAILED runs. When a review of a given head fails (for example the sandbox rejects an oversized PR, or the engine errors deterministically), every later TaskRun save that carries the same pr_url re-fires process_inbox_pr_review. The dedupe finds no live run, so each refire falls through to _supersede_prior_runs and creates a fresh QUEUED run. Each run re-provisions a sandbox and spends an LLM review on the same head. The webhook leg is bounded by real pushes, but the receiver leg fires on every TaskRun output save, and the follow-up loop saves repeatedly while it babysits the PR. There is no equivalent of the LABEL-mode cooldown (STAMPHOG_LABEL_REREVIEW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS) to bound this.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Bound repeat runs per (pull_request, head_sha). For example, treat a FAILED run as handled unless it is older than a cooldown window, or cap runs per head and log stamphog_inbox_pr_failed_run_skipped when the cap is reached. Mirror the existing per-PR cache cooldown used for label-triggered re-reviews.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim and anchor (tasks.py:1202-1230): the head-keyed dedupe excludes FAILED runs so a deterministically failing head is re-reviewed on every refire with no cooldown.

fresh_votes.evidence: Traced the receiver leg from its callers. (1) The refire volume premise is wrong: `handle_task_run_saved` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-89) drops any save whose `update_fields` does not include `output` before touching the DB. The CI follow-up loop (products/tasks/backend/temporal/task_management/workflow.py:1256-1332) never writes `output`; it dispatches a child follow-up message, and its persistence goes through `update_task_run_status` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/update_task_run_status.py:69, `update_fields=["status","error_message","completed_at","updated_at"]`) and `mutate_state_atomic` (products/tasks/backend/models.py:1263, `update_fields=["state","updated_at"]`). Neither reaches `process_inbox_pr_review`. The loop is also hard-bounded: `CI_FOLLOW_UP_DELAY = 15 min`, `MAX_CI_REPETITIONS = 3` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/constants.py:57,60), and it only fires on a PR fingerprint change (workflow.py:1300-1305). (2) The in-repo `output` writers are all bounded per run: `set_task_run_output` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2153-2154, once at completion), the caller PATCH with an `output` key (api.py:2040-2075), and the webhook backstop `_record_run_output_field` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:279-296), which is idempotent per key (returns False when the key is already set). So a deterministically failing head sees a handful of refires, not a stream. (3) Once the PR closes/merges, refires exit at tasks.py:1163-1166 (`stamphog_inbox_pr_not_open`) before the dedupe. (4) Excluding FAILED from the head-keyed dedupe is a documented, tested design choice: the docstring at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1125-1129 and the parametrized case `failed_run_recreated_on_refire` in products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:979,986,997-1000 state that a FAILED run must not count as handled so a single-commit PR whose only review died is not stranded without a verdict. A cooldown/cap as suggested would strand exactly that case; the LABEL cooldown (tasks.py:78,1093-1095) exists for a human-repeatable action with webhook redelivery behind it, which this leg does not have (tasks.py:1152-1154).
fresh_votes.refutation: The finding claims unbounded re-creation of FAILED-head runs driven by the follow-up loop's saves. The code contradicts the premise: the receiver only processes `output`-bearing saves, the follow-up loop never writes `output`, and the loop itself runs at most 3 times at 15-minute intervals. Remaining `output` saves are one-shot or key-idempotent, so a deterministically broken head costs a small bounded number of failed attempts, each of which the code deliberately allows so a transiently failed sole review self-heals on the next save. This is a designed trade-off with a test pinning it, not a defect. The agent-server side (`@posthog/agent`, not present in the worktree) could not be inspected, but even a PATCH per agent turn is bounded by the 3-turn CI cap plus user follow-ups, which does not reach the "unbounded" bar the finding relies on.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Worktree: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215

1. The finding's driver ("the follow-up loop saves repeatedly while it babysits the PR") is contradicted by the receiver's fire gate. products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-89 drops any save whose `update_fields` does not include "output" before touching the DB. The CI follow-up loop in products/tasks/backend/temporal/execute_sandbox/workflow.py writes only through `_update_task_run_status` (lines 464, 580, 625, 1287-1313), which persists via products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/update_task_run_status.py:69 `task_run.save(update_fields=["status", "error_message", "completed_at", "updated_at"])` and `update_state_atomic` (state only). Neither carries "output", so none of those saves re-fire `process_inbox_pr_review`.

2. The only `TaskRun.output` writers are bounded per agent action, not looping: products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2040-2045 (agent-server PATCH output merge), api.py:2154 `set_task_run_output` (one structured-output save), and products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:276-296 `_record_run_output_field`, which is explicitly idempotent (returns False at line 284 and 289 when the key is already set, so `pr_url`/`pr_merged` are written at most once each).

3. Recreating a run after a FAILED one at the same head is the documented, tested contract, not an oversight. products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:979 parametrizes `(ReviewRunStatus.FAILED, "sha-1", "new", 2)` under id `failed_run_recreated_on_refire`, and the test comment at lines 995-999 states: "A FAILED run doesn't count as handled: the refire recreates it, so a single-commit PR whose one review died isn't permanently stranded without a verdict." The task docstring at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1124-1128 documents the same-head refire semantics, and the dedupe comment at tasks.py:1199-1202 explains the intent.

4. Each fire is still serialized and single-run: tasks.py:1203-1209 takes `select_for_update` on runs at (pull_request, head_sha) and tasks.py:1222 `_supersede_prior_runs` guarantees at most one live run per PR, so concurrent fires cannot fan out.

5. The cited LABEL cooldown (tasks.py:76-78, 284-285, 1092-1095) guards a human-repeatable action (label toggle, unbounded by design); the inbox leg is gated by a handful of one-time output writes per run, so there is no equivalent unbounded trigger to bound.
fresh_votes.refutation: The claim needs an unbounded stream of same-head refires against a FAILED run. The code shows that stream does not exist: the receiver ignores every save that does not declare "output" in update_fields (receivers.py:85-89), and the follow-up loop only writes status/state fields (update_task_run_status.py:69). The remaining output writers fire once per unique event (PR detected, structured output set, webhook pr_url/pr_merged recorded idempotently at webhooks.py:284-289). So a deterministically failing head sees at most a few retries over the run's life, each already serialized by the row lock and `_supersede_prior_runs`. Excluding FAILED from the dedupe is deliberate and covered by `test_inbox_receiver_leg_refires_dedupe_on_the_current_head[failed_run_recreated_on_refire]` (test_tasks.py:979, 995-999): it is what recovers a review that died on a transient error without requiring a new push. Adding a per-head cap or cooldown would trade a bounded, rare cost for stranding single-commit PRs whose only review attempt hit a transient failure. The finding's premise is contradicted by the code and the behavior it flags is an intentional, tested design choice, so it is not a real defect.
